notes: The frozen clock starts at 2026-11-06 12:00 IST, but the pipeline's as_of (18:08) is later, so asOf() stays at 18:08 for the whole run. On production asOf() moves every 30 s, so a cache keyed on it rolls over within 30 s; here the same keys live for their full 60 s. The lag figures below are therefore upper bounds for production.
officerC is moved to PWD-WRD in the throwaway durable file only: no test officer's department has a severe open incident.

Only four grievance events in the snapshot link to a complaint in the complaints table. For the other incidents a complaint row owned by citizenA is added to the throwaway durable file, with the number the pipeline's grievance event holds, so the tracker reads it the real way. The real links are checked as well (realComplaints below).
ASSISTANT_TOOLS_API=1 turns on the developer route that runs one assistant tool; it is off by default in production.

sequences.name: resolve, reopen, resolve within two minutes
sequences.why: decisions route: "a double click sends the same decision twice: the one just made ... is kept, not recorded". The third call is not a double click: the latest decision is reopen.

sequences.name: reopen, resolve, reopen within two minutes
sequences.why: the same rule, the other way round

sequences.name: resolve, then a note
sequences.why: effective.ts: "The latest decision other than a note decides"

sequences.name: resolve, then escalate
sequences.why: effective.ts: "verify and escalate leave the status as it is (a verify after a resolve therefore shows the pipeline's status, as the list does)". So the console reopens it; the officer's stage ignores escalate, so the officer still sees it verified.

sequences.name: severe: resolve, then verify
sequences.why: effective.ts names this case: a verify after a resolve shows the pipeline's status

sequences.name: officer close, then the Collector reopens
sequences.why: officer/data.ts: "The latest of those wins"; the Collector's Send back is a reopen

sequences.name: verify a severe incident the pipeline has not verified
sequences.why: verify leaves the status; the list's verified filter should hold it (next check)

sequences.name: officer send, then the Collector verifies: My Tasks
sequences.why: intel.ts: a report sent "always comes to My Tasks ... until the Collector decides"

sequences.name: officer send, send back, officer send, send back, within two minutes
bad: stage: sent, wanted action; My Tasks: 1, wanted 0; the second Send back answered 201 and was not recorded
sequences.why: the same double-click rule, reached with the screens' own buttons: the second Send back is a new decision on a new report, not a double click

sequences.name: reopen an incident the pipeline closed, then the officer sends a report: My Tasks
bad: My Tasks: 1, wanted 2; awaiting list: 0, wanted 1
sequences.why: intel.ts: "Such a report always comes to My Tasks (the officer asked for the Collector's check), whatever the period". sentByOfficer() reads the pipeline's i.is_open

sequences.name: verify, then the list's verified filter
sequences.why: intel.ts overlay sets verified on the row; the list's filter reads the pipeline's i.verified only
